claims.claim: Some early-career hiring may be under disproportionate pressure in AI-exposed work.
claims.counterevidence: Yale macro null; Danish adoption-linked null through 2024; pretrends, education and employer-panel selection.
claims.open_bridge: AI causation versus other shocks, India/UK transfer and effects on established engineers.
claims.test: Compare actual adoption-linked cohorts, hiring/separations, geography and observation windows; avoid interpreting the Stanford19percent gap as19percent of all jobs destroyed.

claims.claim: AI increases software throughput in some contexts while adding time in others.
claims.counterevidence: Different tools/years, tasks, estimands, adoption compliance, review and quality proxies.
claims.open_bridge: Task throughput does not establish total project output, customer value, labor demand or safe long-term code quality.
claims.test: Verify full Cui IV versus ITT design, METR denominator and follow-up selection before using headline effect sizes.

claims.claim: Longer model task horizons could change work allocation substantially by2031.
claims.counterevidence: 50percent success thresholds, unmeasured human baselines, distribution choice, correction sensitivity and production context gaps.
claims.open_bridge: Capability curves do not directly predict replacement of complete jobs or high-reliability deployment dates.
claims.test: Use latest completed horizon/economic-task audit and raw-data provenance. January2026 doubling assumptions are not current calibrated whole-job predictions; never invent p80/p95 or extrapolate unsupported long tasks.

claims.claim: Production integration, verification and domain ownership may remain valuable complements to stronger AI.
claims.evidence_type: cross-field inference, selected current role requirements
claims.counterevidence: The same work can be automated, bundled by vendors or concentrated in few experts; integration can be low-margin consulting.
claims.open_bridge: Current difficulty is not durable scarcity or proof of future hiring volume.
claims.test: Seek prospective autonomous integrations, closed-loop repair and vendor-native governance; compare total cost and paid adoption with human-led baseline.

claims.claim: Robotics platform/runtime/observability work may be a reachable adjacent path for a broad software/ML engineer.
claims.evidence_type: operational data, technical methods, illustrative vacancies
claims.counterevidence: Onsite geography, seniority, C++/real-time requirements, physical validation and safety; simulation does not establish field competence.
claims.open_bridge: No verified assessment of the reader's hardware/math/control depth, and no representative vacancy sample.
claims.test: Separate platform, perception, controls, autonomy research and field roles; test a reproducible typed-state and recovery project against real role criteria.

claims.claim: Energy, industrial and scientific adoption could create valuable software work around physical bottlenecks.
claims.evidence_type: deployment and survey evidence plus commercial inference
claims.counterevidence: Capital intensity, procurement, data rights, vendor concentration, no budget despite need, and low product margins.
claims.open_bridge: Need versus funded buyer and scalable product, operating assets versus announced capacity.
claims.test: Trace a concrete operational decision to a budget owner, existing solution, measurable accepted outcome and procurement route.

claims.claim: Some clinical AI improves specified workflows or diagnostic endpoints.
claims.counterevidence: Device counts are not outcomes; MASAI interval-cancer reduction not statistically established; scribe total time may be mismeasured; drug safety endpoints and small arms.
claims.open_bridge: Patient benefit, long-term safety, external validity and scaled commercial employment.
claims.test: Use prospective outcome endpoints, confidence intervals and total workflow time, with replication and failure capture.

claims.claim: Delegated authority, identity and containment are substantive engineering needs for deployed agents.
claims.evidence_type: technical red-team evidence, standards activity, incident evidence
claims.counterevidence: Lab ASR is not production frequency; threat-model access varies; cloud IAM may absorb product demand.
claims.open_bridge: Skill demand does not automatically establish a new venture category or large accessible vacancy pool.
claims.test: Inspect real threat models and incidents, compare native cloud controls, and test scoped authority under adaptive attack and tool changes.

claims.claim: Cross-field breadth is useful when anchored by demonstrated technical depth and a real domain.
claims.counterevidence: Specialist credential filters and shallow breadth can block access; transfer across fields may be overstated.
claims.open_bridge: Unknown current competence, learning time, desired geography, resources and preferred work style.
claims.test: Offer reversible depth experiments with measurable gates and opportunity costs rather than choosing identity from interests.

claims.claim: Quantum, nuclear/fusion, BCI and wearables deserve selective exploration rather than an automatic career pivot.
claims.evidence_type: technical progress versus deployment and business uncertainty
claims.counterevidence: A major scalable breakthrough or accessible employer platform could accelerate demand; conservative advice can miss asymmetric opportunities.
claims.open_bridge: Precise attainable software layer, prerequisites and opportunity cost for this user.
claims.test: Find concrete open tooling, current role requirements, credible30/90day proof project and decision threshold before recommending investment.
